meta.scene_summary: We are busy building a more secure, distributed future while the house we currently live in is actively being set on fire.

cooking.headline: Temporal raises $550M because distributed systems are hard
cooking.summary: Temporal just hit a $12.55B valuation for ensuring your background jobs actually finish instead of disappearing into the void. Apparently, paying a premium to avoid debugging race conditions at 3 AM is the most profitable business model on earth.
cooking.plain_english: Temporal raised $550 million to help companies manage complex software workflows that involve multiple steps and potential failures.

cooking.headline: Apple finally lets you trade Siri for an assistant that actually listens
cooking.summary: Apple is letting you swap Siri out for ChatGPT or Claude, effectively admitting that their own AI is just a placeholder for a better one. It's like being forced to use the school's default browser before finally being allowed to install Chrome.
cooking.plain_english: Apple is updating its system to allow users to replace the default Siri assistant with third-party artificial intelligence services.

cooking.headline: Ubuntu swaps C for Rust in coreutils, officially making 'memory safe' the new personality trait.
cooking.summary: Canonical finally finished porting the foundation of your terminal to Rust, proving that rewrite-it-in-Rust isn't just a meme. It's a great move for safety, even if your legacy shell scripts will still find creative ways to break anyway.
cooking.plain_english: Ubuntu has completed the process of replacing its core system tools with versions written in the Rust programming language to improve security and performance.

cooking.headline: The US government is speedrunning the 'hire anywhere but here' challenge
cooking.summary: Adding a $100k fee to H-1B visas is a bold strategy if the goal is to convince every tech company to stop hiring in the US entirely. It's like charging a cover fee to a party you're actively trying to clear out.
cooking.plain_english: A new $100,000 fee for H-1B work visas is causing many technology companies to move their hiring operations to other countries.

cooking.headline: Signal finally lets you ditch the phone number, because your digits are just baggage anyway.
cooking.summary: Signal is moving to zero-knowledge proofs so you can stop handing your phone number out like a business card at a networking event. It's the ultimate privacy upgrade for people who treat their phone number like a state secret.
cooking.plain_english: Signal is updating its registration process to allow users to sign up without providing a phone number by using advanced cryptographic verification methods.

cooked.headline: Chess.com gets checkmated by scrapers, proving that even grandmasters can't defend against a public API.
cooked.summary: Over 7 million users had their data leaked because someone decided that scraping the entire site was easier than actually learning how to play the game. It's the digital equivalent of losing your queen in the first three moves because you were too busy looking at your phone.
cooked.plain_english: A data breach involving 7.3 million Chess.com user accounts occurred due to unauthorized automated data collection from the website.

cooked.headline: Microsoft patches Windows and breaks the only three things you actually do
cooked.summary: Microsoft pushed an update to fix security holes, but somehow managed to disable audio, remote access, and the ability to copy-paste. It is truly an impressive feat to make a computer less functional than a paperweight during a routine maintenance check.
cooked.plain_english: A recent software update from Microsoft has caused audio, remote access, and copy-paste functions to stop working on Windows and Excel.

cooked.headline: OpenAI bots were apparently lurking in RubyGems, watching the house burn down.
cooked.summary: It turns out OpenAI's bots were aware of a RubyGems caching vulnerability while everyone else was still trying to figure out why their builds were acting possessed. It's comforting to know the AI is smart enough to spot a security hole, but apparently too polite to mention it until the party is over.
cooked.plain_english: OpenAI's automated systems identified a security vulnerability in the RubyGems package repository before it was publicly disclosed.

cooked.headline: Manufacturers accidentally granted every Android app root access to your device
cooked.summary: OEMs somehow managed to leave a backdoor open that lets any random app take full control of your phone. It is essentially the digital equivalent of leaving your house keys in the front door lock and hoping nobody notices.
cooked.plain_english: A security vulnerability in several Android smartphones allows applications to gain administrative control over the device without the user's permission.

cooked.headline: TikTok lied about child safety, proving their 'parental controls' were just a suggestion
cooked.summary: A Texas judge ruled that TikTok misled parents about their child safety features, which is a bold strategy for a company that already lives in a glass house. It turns out the safety settings were about as effective as a 'do not touch' sign on a toddler's favorite toy.
cooked.plain_english: A court ruled that TikTok provided false information regarding the effectiveness of its safety tools designed to protect children on the platform.
